description: We are the team Crimson Amalthea, united by different skills and interests to create an interactive and FPS-explorable outpost 3D game. Our team has 5 members handling coding, 3D modelling, and planning for the core gameplay, plus a researcher and a narrative designer. We all love space and want to make mission design less intimidating and more hands-on.
summary:
The game focuses on maintaining a Mars base, managing resources, and uncovering the first expedition's unfinished work. Each day, players check life-support systems, inspect equipment, and make repairs when necessary.

Food production combines indoor farming, fungal cultivation, and bioprocessing. Players grow crops, monitor fungi, and turn organic leftovers into nutrients. A nuclear reactor supplies electricity. During solar events, players activate experimental magnetic shielding while protecting essential systems. Dust storms reduce solar output, making battery reserves important. A MOXIE-inspired system extracts oxygen from Martian carbon dioxide. Players manage its power, monitor oxygen storage, and repair faults.

Three rovers each have two expeditions, making six missions. They explore automatically but lose health from terrain hazards and malfunctions. Damage slows progress. Players decide whether to continue or recall a rover. At zero health, it becomes disabled and must be retrieved for repairs. Minigames determine repair difficulty and needed parts. Repaired rovers can resume missions.

While rovers explore, players maintain the base. Expeditions provide scientific findings, samples, and environmental data, while unlocking locations and story clues. Gaps in the astronaut's reports gradually reveal what happened during the first expedition and what lies beneath Mars.
details:
Project Overview

Our project is a Mars survival and exploration game that allows players to experience the challenges of maintaining a human settlement on Mars. The game revolves around managing essential resources such as electricity, food, oxygen, and water while maintaining the base's life-support systems and conducting exploration missions. Players oversee three rovers, each assigned two expeditions, to explore different locations, collect scientific data, and gradually uncover the unfinished work and mysteries of the first expedition.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project provides both educational and entertainment benefits by introducing players to concepts related to space exploration, sustainability, resource management, and scientific technology. It also encourages the development of critical thinking, problem-solving, strategic planning, and decision-making skills. Our intended impact is to increase awareness and interest in space exploration while helping players understand the challenges of establishing and maintaining human life beyond Earth.

Tools, Programming Languages, and Software Used

For development, our team used Blender to create all the 3D models and visual assets for the game. We used Visual Studio Code (VS Code) as our primary code editor and Claude as an AI-assisted tool to help polish and improve certain aspects of our work. Our project utilized Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, CSS, and HTML for programming and development. AI was used only for assistance in refining and improving our work, not for developing the actual game or creating its core mechanics.

Creativity and Innovation

What makes our project creative is its combination of survival simulation, resource management, rover exploration, repair minigames, and a mystery-driven storyline. Rather than focusing solely on exploration or survival, players must balance maintaining the Mars base with completing scientific expeditions. The integration of science-inspired technologies, such as MOXIE-inspired oxygen production, nuclear power management, and bioprocessing, also adds depth to the gameplay. Furthermore, the mystery surrounding the first expedition gives players an additional objective beyond simply surviving.

Factors Considered During Development

Throughout development, our team prioritized scientific accuracy, gameplay balance, technical feasibility, player engagement, visual design, and overall user experience. We made sure to base the game's scientific information and concepts on NASA-approved data and reliable scientific sources to keep the gameplay as realistic and scientifically grounded as possible. We also considered how each gameplay system would interact with the others, ensuring that resource management, exploration, and equipment maintenance would provide meaningful challenges without making the game unnecessarily complicated.

Overall, our goal is to create an educational yet entertaining experience that combines scientific accuracy, creativity, and interactive gameplay to encourage curiosity about Mars, technology, and the future of human space exploration.
